name: Aalto Robot Learning (Joni Pajarinen)
summary: The lab works on reinforcement learning for robots, including exploration, multi-objective and offline meta-RL, and decision making under partial observability.
question: How can autonomous robots learn to accomplish complex tasks in unstructured environments?

name: Aaron Courville group (Aaron Courville)
primary: deep RL and RL for LLMs
summary: The group works on deep learning with a substantial deep-RL line, including RL fine-tuning of language models and architecture and scaling studies for deep RL agents.
question: How can deep networks be trained with reinforcement learning to scale and to solve hard problems?

teamMembers.role: PhD student; co-supervisor Pablo Samuel Castro

teamMembers.name: Esra’a Saleh
teamMembers.role: PhD student; primary supervisor Glen Berseth

name: Aarti Singh group (Aarti Singh)
summary: The group studies interactive and sequential learning, including reinforcement learning from text feedback, RLVR dynamics and multi-objective RL.
question: How can learners use richer, adaptive feedback to learn decisions efficiently?

name: Adam White group (Adam White)
summary: The group models intelligence as an RL agent continually interacting with an unknown environment, with work on continual-learning testbeds, recurrent agents, actor-critic design and RL for industrial control.
question: How can intelligence be modelled as a reinforcement-learning agent that continually interacts with an unknown environment and learns from a scalar reward?

name: Adam Wierman group
primary: robust and safe RL for systems
summary: Develops RL and learning-augmented control with provable guarantees (robust constrained MDPs, safe sim-to-real, multi-agent RL) for networked systems.
question: How can learning-based control be made provably robust for the networked systems that govern society?

name: Adaptive & Intelligent Robotics Lab – AIRL (Antoine Cully)
summary: Develops quality-diversity and evolutionary RL algorithms that let robots discover diverse skills and adapt to new situations.
question: How can physical robots autonomously adapt to new and unforeseen situations, such as a new environment, task or damage?

name: Adaptive Generalist Learning Lab (André Biedenkapp)
summary: The group develops contextual reinforcement learning methods for adaptable, generalist policies and applies RL to dynamic algorithm configuration.
question: How can giving RL agents contextual information about their environment make policies generalise when conditions change?

name: Adaptive Systems Laboratory (Ali H. Sayed)
summary: Analyses adaptation and learning over networks of agents, including multi-agent policy optimization and RL under partial observability.
question: How can networks of adaptive agents with learning abilities cooperate and learn in uncertain environments?

name: Advanced Networking and System Research Lab (John C. S. Lui)
institution: The Chinese University of Hong Kong (Department of Computer Science and Engineering)
summary: Among networking and systems topics, the lab works on online learning algorithms, including multi-armed and dueling bandits, model-based RL and quantum algorithms for MDPs.
question: How can online learning algorithms such as bandits and reinforcement learning be made efficient for networked systems?

name: Agent Mediated Intelligence Research Group (Bo An)
institution: Nanyang Technological University (College of Computing and Data Science)
summary: The group works on multi-agent systems, computational game theory and reinforcement learning, recently including RL for LLM-based agents.
question: How can game theory and reinforcement learning produce effective decision-making for multiple interacting agents?

name: Agile Robotics and Perception Lab (Giuseppe Loianno)
primary: deep RL for agile aerial robots
summary: Develops perception, learning and control for agile aerial robots, including fast deep-RL tooling (RLtools) for continuous control.
question: How can agile robots navigate complex, dynamic environments using only onboard sensing and learned control?

teamMembers.name: Luca Morando
teamMembers.role: Postdoctoral researcher, NYU; visiting postdoc at UC Berkeley

teamMembers.name: Jiuhong Xiao
teamMembers.role: PhD student, NYU; visiting student researcher at UC Berkeley

name: AI & Reinforcement Learning Lab (AIRe) (Aviral Kumar)
primary: scaling RL; offline RL; RL for LLMs
summary: Builds reinforcement learning and sequential decision-making algorithms, from value-based and offline RL to RL training of language models and real robots.
question: How can reinforcement learning be scaled to train AI systems that act autonomously in open-world settings?

researchPlans.title: Some Perspectives on Reinforcement Learning Research
researchPlans.author: Aviral Kumar

researchPlans.title: Some Perspectives on Reinforcement Learning Research
researchPlans.author: Aviral Kumar

name: AI for decision-making – Information Systems group (Yingqian Zhang; Hendrik Baier)
summary: Applies deep and programmatic RL to scheduling, routing and other combinatorial optimization problems in logistics and manufacturing.
question: How can data-driven decision-making methods such as deep RL solve operational optimization problems reliably and interpretably?

name: AI for People and Society group – Francisco S. Melo (INESC-ID)
summary: Melo's group develops reinforcement-learning and decision-theoretic planning methods for agents that interact with other agents, including ad hoc teamwork, value-decomposition MARL and risk-aware MDPs.
question: How can autonomous agents learn and plan to interact with other agents, human or artificial, in complex and possibly unknown environments?

name: Ai2 OLMo post-training (Hanna Hajishirzi)
institution: Allen Institute for AI (Ai2); University of Washington
summary: Develops fully open post-training recipes for OLMo models, including reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards and scalable verifiable RL environments.
question: How can open language models be post-trained with reinforcement learning on verifiable rewards in a fully reproducible way?

name: AIR-DREAM Lab (Xianyuan Zhan)
institution: Tsinghua University (Institute for AI Industry Research, AIR)
summary: The lab develops data-driven decision-making methods, mainly offline and real-world RL and imitation learning, for embodied AI, autonomous driving and industrial control.
question: How can learning-based, data-driven decision-making be made robust, generalizable and deployable in real-world settings?

name: Akshat Kumar group (Akshat Kumar)
institution: Singapore Management University (School of Computing and Information Systems)
summary: The group develops safe, constrained and offline RL methods and multi-agent planning techniques.
question: How can agents learn policies that satisfy constraints and safety requirements from limited or offline data?

name: Alan Fern group
summary: Studies RL and planning, including offline safe RL and learned action ranking, and RL for bipedal robot locomotion.
question: How can agents combine learning and planning to make safe, effective sequential decisions?

name: Aldo Pacchiano group (Aldo Pacchiano)
institution: Boston University; Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
summary: The group studies exploration, model selection, multi-policy evaluation and reward design in reinforcement learning and bandits.
question: How can agents explore and evaluate policies efficiently when objectives and models are uncertain?

name: Alessandra Russo (Imperial College London)
summary: Develops neuro-symbolic and logic-based methods for RL, including learned task structures, skill transfer and environment design.
question: How can symbolic and neuro-symbolic learning make agents robust, interpretable and explainable?

name: Alexander Rakhlin group (Alexander Rakhlin)
summary: The group develops statistical and computational theory for interactive decision making, including reinforcement learning, bandits and outcome-based RL for language models.
question: What are the fundamental statistical limits of learning to make decisions interactively?

name: Alexandre Proutiere (KTH Decision and Control Systems)
summary: Proutiere works on statistically optimal algorithms for bandits and reinforcement learning, including low-rank and hierarchical zero-shot RL and diffusion-based model-based RL.
question: What are the statistically optimal ways to learn and control in reinforcement-learning and bandit problems, and how do they apply to networked systems?

name: Amazon Frontier AI & Robotics (Pieter Abbeel)
summary: Develops RL methods and data pipelines for humanoid control, including fast off-policy sim-to-real locomotion training and interaction-preserving motion retargeting.
question: How can humanoid robots learn whole-body skills quickly in simulation and transfer them to hardware?

name: Ambuj Tewari group (Ambuj Tewari)
summary: The group develops bandit and reinforcement learning algorithms, including average-reward linear MDPs and adaptive interventions in mobile health.
question: How can sequential decision algorithms personalise interventions efficiently and reliably?

name: Amir-massoud Farahmand group (Amir-massoud Farahmand)
institution: Polytechnique Montréal; Mila; University of Toronto (status-only)
summary: The group studies the computational and statistical mechanisms of efficient RL agents, including decision-aware model learning, policy optimisation and plasticity in continual RL.
question: What computational and statistical mechanisms are required to design efficient RL agents that adaptively improve their long-term performance?

researchPlans.title: Research Statement: Rethinking Reinforcement Learning
researchPlans.author: Amir-massoud Farahmand

name: Amos Storkey Group (Amos Storkey)
summary: Works on data-efficient and multi-agent RL, including analyses of memory and Markov assumptions in cooperative MARL benchmarks.
question: How can learning systems, including multi-agent RL agents, learn efficiently and continually?

name: Amsterdam Machine Learning Lab – van Hoof group (Herke van Hoof)
summary: Studies data-efficient RL, including replay correction, task composition and policies that generalize across instructions and tasks.
question: How can RL agents learn efficiently by reusing structure across tasks?

name: Anastasios Lekkas (NTNU Engineering Cybernetics)
institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
summary: Lekkas's group applies deep reinforcement learning and explainable AI to guidance, navigation and control of surface and underwater vessels, including field trials.
question: How can AI methods such as reinforcement learning be merged with control engineering to give marine cyber-physical systems more autonomy?

name: Andrea Zanette group
summary: Studies reinforcement learning for training and aligning foundation models, including variance reduction and efficiency in RL post-training of reasoning models.
question: How can reinforcement learning make foundation-model reasoning more efficient and better aligned?

name: Andrew G. Barto research programme
summary: Studies the relationship between reinforcement learning and neuroscience, including brain reward signals and biologically plausible learning rules.

name: APEX Lab RL group (Weinan Zhang)
institution: Shanghai Jiao Tong University (School of Computer Science)
summary: The group works on reinforcement learning, agentic AI and embodied AI, including on-policy RL with generative policies and humanoid whole-body control.
question: How can reinforcement learning make AI agents and embodied systems learn effective decisions from interaction?

name: Applied and Theoretical Aspects of Robot Intelligence Lab (Majid Khadiv)
summary: Combines optimal control and machine learning for legged and humanoid robots, generating motions with trajectory optimization and transferring them to hardware through RL tracking policies.
question: How can robots autonomously plan in new situations and continually improve their skills in the real world?

name: Applied Artificial Intelligence Lab – A2I (Ingmar Posner)
summary: Studies robot learning with world models, off-policy actor-critic methods and learning from demonstration, including benchmarks for continual world-model learning.
question: How can robots that operate in complex real-world settings keep improving through use in their own workspace?

name: Applied Computational Psychiatry Lab (Quentin Huys)
summary: Uses reinforcement-learning models of behaviour to study mechanisms, prediction and treatment of mental illness.
question: How are the brain's computational and learning functions affected in mental illness, and can this understanding yield clinical tools?

name: Applied Probability / RL Theory Group (Leif Döring)
summary: The group studies the mathematics of reinforcement learning, including convergence of policy gradient methods and the role of target networks in Q-learning.
question: What rigorous insight into the stochastic foundations of reinforcement learning can bring algorithmic improvements?

name: Applied Technical-Cognitive Systems (J. Marius Zöllner)
institution: Karlsruhe Institute of Technology / FZI Research Center for Information Technology
summary: The group works on perception and behaviour decision for autonomous vehicles and robots, including distributional and expert-guided reinforcement learning for safe driving.
question: How can technical-cognitive systems such as autonomous vehicles understand situations and decide on behaviour reliably?

name: ARIA Lab (Daniel S. Brown)
summary: Studies reward inference from human input, robust policy optimization from demonstrations and performance bounds for robot learning.
question: How can robots infer what humans want and act safely under reward uncertainty?

researchPlans.title: Research Statement
researchPlans.author: Daniel S. Brown

name: Articulated Robotics Group / Dynamic Robot Systems (Ioannis Havoutis)
summary: Trains and deploys RL controllers for quadruped locomotion and loco-manipulation alongside model-based motion optimisation.
question: How can walking robots generate robust, dynamic motion and be deployed in practical field settings?

name: Artificial Cognitive Systems Lab (Marcel van Gerven)
summary: Connects learning, inference and control in natural and artificial systems, including reward-modulated learning rules and recurrent RL policies.
question: Which computational mechanisms support learning, inference and control in natural and artificial systems?

researchPlans.title: The neuroconnectionist research programme
researchPlans.author: Adrien Doerig; Rowan Sommers; Katja Seeliger; Blake Richards; Jenann Ismael; Grace Lindsay; Konrad Kording; Talia Konkle; Marcel A. J. van Gerven; Nikolaus Kriegeskorte; Tim C. Kietzmann

name: Artificial Intelligence and Formal Methods – AI-FM (Nils Jansen)
summary: The group combines reinforcement learning with formal verification, working on shielded safe RL and policies for partially observable and uncertain models.
question: How can machine learning be combined with formal verification to give AI systems that are safe, robust and dependable?

name: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Chair (Eyke Hüllermeier)
summary: The chair works on preference-based reinforcement learning and RL from human feedback, reward modelling and multi-task bandits.
question: How can learning systems use preference feedback and quantified uncertainty to learn reliably, for example in RL from human feedback?

name: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning group (Anders Jonsson)
summary: The group studies sequential decision problems for one or several agents, combining reinforcement learning with automated planning and hierarchical problem structure.
question: How can agents find and exploit structure, hierarchy and planning to solve single- and multi-agent sequential decision problems efficiently?

name: Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Lab (Kristian Kersting)
summary: The lab works on neurosymbolic and interpretable deep reinforcement learning, such as pretraining with logical options and evaluating RL agents against human-level generalisation.
question: How can statistical learning and symbolic reasoning be combined so that agents understand complex worlds and act responsibly?

name: Artificial Intelligence and Probabilistic Reasoning Lab (AIPR) (Kee-Eung Kim)
institution: KAIST (Kim Jaechul Graduate School of AI)
summary: The lab develops reinforcement learning, imitation learning and RL-based fine-tuning methods for sequential decision-making and language models.
question: How can agents learn good sequential decisions from rewards, demonstrations and preferences?

name: Artificial Intelligence Lab Brussels – RL (Ann Nowé; Diederik M. Roijers)
summary: Works on multi-agent and multi-objective RL and on distilling deep RL policies into interpretable models.
question: How can RL agents handle multiple objectives and multiple agents while remaining interpretable?

name: Asuman Ozdaglar group (Asuman Ozdaglar)
summary: The group studies optimisation and multi-agent learning, including policy-gradient methods for games and RL on graph-structured MDPs.
question: How do learning agents reach good outcomes when they interact strategically?

name: Audrey Durand group (Audrey Durand)
summary: The group works on bandits and reinforcement learning, including multi-objective RL, RL fine-tuning of language models and adaptive experimentation.
question: How can bandit and RL algorithms make sample-efficient sequential decisions in real applications?

name: Aurélien Garivier (bandit theory)
summary: Works on the statistics of sequential decision making, including best-arm and best-transition identification and risk-sensitive planning.
question: What are the optimal sample complexities of identification and planning problems in sequential decision making?

name: Automation and Robotics Research Group (Holger Voos)
primary: rl for aerial and space robots
summary: Applies RL, sometimes combined with MPC, to the control of UAVs, manipulators and space robots.
question: How can learning-based control make aerial, space and manipulator robots act autonomously in uncertain conditions?

name: AutoML / AutoRL group (Marius Lindauer)
summary: The group applies AutoML methods to reinforcement learning (AutoRL), studying hyperparameter optimisation, network growth and generalisation of RL agents.
question: How can automating the design decisions in the RL pipeline make reinforcement learning sample-efficient, stable and broadly applicable?

teamMembers.name: Aditya Mohan
teamMembers.role: Reinforcement Learning team member / PhD student

name: Autonomous Agents Research Group (Stefano V. Albrecht)
institution: Nanyang Technological University (College of Computing and Data Science)
summary: The group develops deep and multi-agent reinforcement learning and foundation-model-based agents, working with industry on autonomous driving and warehouse robotics.
question: How can autonomous agents learn, reason and collaborate to accomplish tasks in complex environments?

name: Autonomous Decision and Control Lab (Zachary Sunberg)
primary: POMDPs and decision making under uncertainty
summary: Develops algorithms for sequential decision making under uncertainty, including online POMDP planning, robustness analysis of POMDP policies and tree search for Markov games.
question: How can autonomous systems make sequential decisions under uncertainty, with an uncertainty-first approach?

name: Autonomous Intelligent Systems (Sven Behnke)
summary: The group builds cognitive robots and uses reinforcement learning and latent world-model planning for manipulation and humanoid control.
question: How can cognitive robots act competently in complex, uncertain real-world environments?

name: Autonomous Learning / Distributed Intelligence Group (Georg Martius)
summary: The group studies autonomous learning in embodied agents through intrinsically motivated, model-based and constrained reinforcement learning for robot control.
question: How can an embodied agent decide what to learn, how to learn it and how to judge its own learning success?

name: Autonomous Learning Lab (Bruno Castro da Silva)
summary: Designs general-purpose RL algorithms, including work on plasticity-stability trade-offs, reward selection under limited feedback and diffusion-policy control.
question: How can RL algorithms be made general-purpose and safe enough to solve real-world tasks with little human intervention?

name: Autonomous Learning Robots Lab – ALR (Gerhard Neumann)
summary: The lab develops machine learning methods for robotics, including episodic and off-policy reinforcement learning, diffusion-based maximum-entropy RL and imitation learning.
question: Which machine learning methods let robots learn versatile skills efficiently from interaction and demonstrations?

name: Autonomous Multi-Robots Lab (Javier Alonso-Mora)
summary: Develops planning and learning methods for teams of mobile robots, including multi-agent RL for cooperative aerial manipulation.
question: How can teams of autonomous robots navigate, coordinate and act safely in dynamic environments shared with humans?

teamMembers.name: Sihao Sun
teamMembers.role: Researcher; PI of the VENI aerial manipulation project

name: Autonomous Robots Lab (Kostas Alexis)
institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
summary: The lab develops resilient autonomous robots and uses deep reinforcement learning for navigation, active perception and legged locomotion.
question: How can autonomous robots operate resiliently over long periods in complex and degraded environments?

name: Autonomous Systems Group (Ufuk Topcu)
institution: The University of Texas at Austin
summary: The group combines formal methods, control and reinforcement learning to build autonomous systems with safety guarantees, including constrained RL curricula and POMDPs under model uncertainty.
question: How can autonomous systems learn while providing verifiable safety guarantees?

name: Autonomous Systems Lab (Dongheui Lee)
summary: Develops robot learning methods, including real-world RL for contact-rich manipulation and RL with model-based supervision for torque-controlled locomotion.
question: How can robots acquire new motor skills autonomously, building on observation of human behaviour?

name: Autonomous Vision Group (Andreas Geiger)
summary: The group works on perception and sensorimotor control for autonomous systems, including reinforcement learning of driving planning policies with simple rewards and RL post-training in simulation.
question: How can autonomous systems such as self-driving cars become more autonomous, efficient, robust and safe?

teamMembers.name: Jovan Cicvarić
teamMembers.role: Part-time Research Engineer, Scholar Inbox; current external ML engineer

name: Balaraman Ravindran group, RBCDSAI (Balaraman Ravindran)
institution: Indian Institute of Technology Madras (RBCDSAI; Department of CSE)
summary: The group works on reinforcement learning, including evaluation of RL policies and online/offline preference optimization, alongside other machine-learning topics.
question: How can reinforcement learning agents be made reliable and efficient to train and evaluate?

name: Baoxiang Wang group (Baoxiang Wang)
institution: The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shenzhen (School of Data Science)
summary: The group studies reinforcement learning and game theory, including learning in games, multi-agent incentives and RL for language models.
question: How do multiple learning agents learn, reason and coordinate in games and under information design?

name: Barry Lab (Caswell Barry; William de Cothi)
summary: Studies hippocampal and subicular predictive maps related to the successor representation, and replay, using rodent recordings and models.
question: How does the hippocampus learn predictive maps of space and experience, and what substrates support this predictive learning?

name: Bei Peng (University of Sheffield)
summary: Works on deep and multi-agent RL, including safe RL and value estimation with flow matching.
question: How can agents learn to achieve complex goals from experience, with or without interacting with humans?

teamMembers.name: Bei Peng
teamMembers.role: Lecturer (Assistant Professor), AI and Applications of AI

name: Benjamin Van Roy group
summary: Studies data-efficient RL, exploration and bandit theory, including RL from pairwise preferences for long-horizon decisions.
question: How can agents learn efficiently by exploring intelligently and learning from feedback?

name: Berkeley Robot Learning Lab (Pieter Abbeel)
summary: Studies scalable deep RL (model-based RL, high-capacity value functions, flow-policy RL) and its use for humanoid and dexterous robot learning.
question: How can robots learn complex skills efficiently through deep reinforcement and imitation learning?

name: Biao Luo group (Biao Luo)
summary: The group works on reinforcement learning and adaptive dynamic programming for intelligent control, including multi-agent and preference-based multi-objective RL and RL-guided molecular design.
question: How can reinforcement learning and adaptive dynamic programming deliver optimal decisions and control in complex systems?

name: Biological Psychology Lab (Jan Peters, Cologne)
summary: The lab studies human reinforcement learning and exploration with computational models, pharmacology and neuroimaging, including model-based control in gambling disorder and RNN agents.
question: How do dopamine and related mechanisms shape exploration and model-based versus model-free control in human decision-making?

name: Biorobotics Laboratory – BioRob (Auke Ijspeert)
summary: Studies animal locomotion control with robots and neuromechanical simulation, and uses RL for whole-body control of salamander-like and legged robots.
question: What neural mechanisms underlie movement control and learning in animals, and how can they inspire robot control?

name: Bo Dai group
institution: Georgia Institute of Technology; Google DeepMind
summary: Develops reinforcement learning and planning methods built on learned representations and generative models of the world.
question: How can agents gain decision-making and planning ability by modeling the world?

name: Bogacz Group (Rafal Bogacz)
institution: University of Oxford (MRC Brain Network Dynamics Unit)
summary: Builds computational models of learning in basal ganglia and cortex, including temporal-difference models of dopamine signals in value learning and habit formation.
question: How do brain networks learn and process information, and how do these dynamics change in neurological disorders?

name: Bogunovic Group (Ilija Bogunovic)
summary: Develops bandit, Bayesian optimization and RL methods that are robust to uncertainty, applied to LLM reasoning, alignment and world-model learning.
question: How can sequential decision-making remain reliable under uncertainty and adversarial conditions, from bandits to training large models?

name: BOLD Lab – British Open-Ended Learning & Discovery (Jakob Foerster)
lead: Jakob Foerster; Tim Rocktäschel; Laura Toni; Anisoara Calinescu
institution: University of Oxford; University College London; Imperial College London
summary: Lab formed in 2026 by merging Oxford's FLAIR and WhiRL, UCL's DARK and LASP and Imperial's AIRL groups, working on open-ended learning, multi-agent RL, meta-learned RL algorithms and agent training environments.
question: How can agents keep learning in open-ended environments that supply novel tasks without reliable reward functions, often by creating their own curricula?

name: Boston Dynamics Atlas learning team
summary: Trains Atlas humanoid behaviours with RL in simulation and from demonstrations, including zero-shot transfer of athletic skills.
question: How can a humanoid robot acquire general, dynamic whole-body behaviours through reinforcement learning and transfer them to hardware?

teamMembers.name: Michael Lutter
teamMembers.role: Technical Manager, Atlas RL Manipulation Team at Boston Dynamics

name: Brain x Machine Intelligence Lab (Sang Wan Lee)
institution: KAIST (Department of Bio and Brain Engineering; Center for Neuroscience-inspired AI)
summary: The lab studies how the brain arbitrates between reinforcement-learning strategies in the prefrontal cortex and striatum, and uses these findings for neuroscience-inspired AI.
question: How does the brain arbitrate between learning strategies to adapt flexibly, and how can this inform AI?

name: Brunton Lab (Steven L. Brunton)
summary: Develops data-driven modelling and control methods (e.g. SINDy) and combines learned dynamics models with control and RL for physical systems.
question: How can models of complex dynamical systems be learned from data and used for control?

name: ByteDance Seed LLM RL (Mingxuan Wang)
summary: Develops open large-scale RL algorithms and systems for reasoning language models, including DAPO and value-augmented PPO (VAPO).
question: How can reinforcement learning for long chain-of-thought reasoning be made stable, efficient and reproducible at scale?

teamMembers.name: Mingxuan Wang
teamMembers.role: Seed research manager / LLM reinforcement-learning co-lead

name: ByteDance Seed Robotics (Hang Li)
summary: Develops GR-series robot policies and GR-RL, which augments a generalist vision-language-action model with reinforcement learning for precise long-horizon manipulation.
question: How can generalist robot policies be turned into reliable specialists for dexterous long-horizon tasks?

name: Böhmer Research Lab (Wendelin Böhmer)
summary: Studies why deep RL agents fail to generalize out of distribution and develops offline, model-based and tree-search methods that transfer better.
question: Which structural choices let deep RL agents generalize beyond the situations they were trained on?

name: CARE.AI Lab (Pradeep Varakantham)
institution: Singapore Management University (School of Computing and Information Systems)
summary: The lab develops collaborative and trustworthy agent systems, with a current focus on trustworthy (safe, robust) reinforcement learning methods.
question: How can reinforcement learning methods be made trustworthy for collaborative intelligent agent systems?

summary: Studies reward learning, assistance games and related decision-theoretic foundations for AI systems that act in humans' interests.
question: How can AI systems be built to be provably beneficial when their objectives are uncertain?

name: Chair of Information-oriented Control (Sandra Hirche)
summary: Develops data-driven and learning-based control with formal guarantees, including continuous-time offline RL and safe exploration via bandits.
question: How can data-driven and learning-based control come with guarantees under uncertainty and limited data?

name: Chair of Robotics, Artificial Intelligence and Real-time Systems (Alois Knoll)
summary: Studies lifelong and meta-reinforcement learning for robots, including preserving and reusing knowledge across tasks and skill priors for long-horizon manipulation.
question: How can robots preserve and combine knowledge across tasks so that they keep acquiring new skills?

institution: Institute of Science and Technology Austria
summary: Studies reinforcement learning with formally specified objectives such as reachability, with PAC and optimality guarantees in MDPs and stochastic games.
question: What guarantees can learning algorithms provide for formally specified objectives in stochastic systems and games?

name: Chi Jin group
summary: Studies the theory and algorithms of reinforcement learning and multi-agent learning, and applies them to LLM reasoning and agents.
question: What makes reinforcement learning and multi-agent learning provably efficient, and how can these ideas improve reasoning agents?

name: Christopher Amato group
summary: Develops principled methods for multi-agent reinforcement learning and planning under uncertainty with limited communication.
question: How can teams of agents coordinate under uncertainty and limited communication?

name: CLAIRE (Caglar Gulcehre)
summary: Works on sample-efficient and offline RL and on RL-based alignment and algorithm discovery with large language models.
question: How can learning algorithms make efficient and safe use of experiential data and weak, sparse or noisy feedback?

name: Cognitive Cooperating Robots Lab (RoCoCo)
summary: The lab works on cognitive robotics and includes reinforcement learning with non-Markovian rewards and multi-agent RL for robots and UAVs.
question: How can cognitive robots combine reasoning and learning, including learning from non-Markovian rewards, to act and cooperate?

name: Cognitive Learning for Vision and Robotics Lab (CLVR) (Joseph J. Lim)
institution: KAIST (Kim Jaechul Graduate School of AI)
summary: The lab develops reinforcement learning and robot learning methods, including reward learning and world-model representations, for sequential decision-making through perception and action.
question: How can intelligent systems make sequential decisions in the world through perception, action and reasoning?

teamMembers.name: Joonkyu Min
teamMembers.role: Undergraduate intern / incoming KAIST MS student

name: Cognitive Robot Autonomy & Learning (CoRAL) Lab (Ahmed H. Qureshi)
summary: Researches learning-based planning and control for robots, including reinforcement and imitation learning for manipulation, navigation and multi-agent tasks.
question: How can robots learn to plan and act autonomously in complex, changing environments?

name: Collaborative AI and Robotics Lab – CLAIR (Sarah Keren)
summary: The lab studies multi-agent environment design, combining model-based decision making under uncertainty with multi-agent reinforcement learning and game theory.
question: How can the environment of a multi-agent AI system be designed so that it complements the agents' capabilities and compensates for their limitations?

name: Computational and Integrative Cognition Lab (Yunzhe Liu)
institution: Chinese Institute for Brain Research, Beijing (CIBR); Beijing Normal University
primary: replay and planning in the brain
summary: The lab studies the neural and computational basis of flexible behaviour in humans, focusing on hippocampal replay, model-based learning and planning, and cognitive maps.
question: How can we learn so much from so little and make flexible decisions in novel contexts?

name: Computational Behavior Lab (Antti Oulasvirta)
summary: The lab builds computational-rationality models of human behaviour, often trained with reinforcement learning, and applies them to interactive systems and RL from human feedback.
question: How can computational models of human behaviour, built on bounded optimal decision making, be used to design interactive and intelligent systems?

name: Computational Cognitive Neuroscience Lab (Samuel Gershman)
institution: Harvard University (Psychology; Center for Brain Science)
summary: The lab combines behavioural, neural and computational methods to study how the brain learns structured models and uses them for reward-guided behaviour under computational limits, including dopamine-based learning and, with Kempner Fellow Wilka Carvalho, continual RL in humans and machines.
question: How does the brain acquire richly structured knowledge from little data and use it to guide adaptive behaviour under stringent computational limits?

name: Computational Cognitive Neuroscience Lab – CCN (Anne Collins)
institution: University of California, Berkeley (Psychology; Helen Wills Neuroscience Institute)
summary: The lab builds and tests computational models of how reinforcement learning interacts with working memory, habits and executive function in human learning.
question: How do multiple brain processes, such as reinforcement learning and working memory, jointly support learning and decision making?

name: Computational Intelligence and Deep Learning group – CIDL (Anastasios Tefas)
primary: deep rl for robotics and trading
summary: The group develops deep reinforcement-learning methods for robotics, UAV localisation and financial trading, with a focus on robustness and data efficiency.
question: How can computational intelligence and deep learning give robots and other agents robust perception and decision making?

name: Computational Minds and Agent Well-Being Laboratory (Philip Thomas)
summary: Works on reinforcement learning with a focus on policy evaluation and safety guarantees, alongside research on computational theories of mind and agent well-being.
question: How can AI systems be designed to optimize task performance while meeting safety guarantees and respecting agent well-being?

name: Computational Neuroscience Group (Sen Cheng)
primary: rl models of memory and navigation
summary: The group builds deep reinforcement learning and neural network models of hippocampal memory and spatial navigation and compares them with animal and human data.
question: How do episodic memory and hippocampal processes support learning and spatial navigation, as seen through reinforcement learning agents?

name: Computational Robot Design & Fabrication Lab – CREATE (Josie Hughes)
summary: Builds tendon-driven and swimming robots and studies sim-to-real transfer of RL policies through better physical models and system identification.
question: How can robots be designed and used differently, with data-driven design and large-scale physical experimentation?

name: Computational Robotics Lab (Stelian Coros)
summary: Studies computational design and control of robots, including RL with simulation-to-real transfer and online fine-tuning on physical hardware.
question: How should future robots be made and controlled so they can operate in complex environments and interact with people?

question: Can scaling self-supervised RL unlock new goal-reaching capabilities?

name: Computer Vision Laboratory – CVLab (Pascal Fua)
summary: Computer vision lab that also develops on-policy RL with expert guidance and preference optimization for physically plausible humanoid motion.
question: How can machines interpret images and recover 3D shape and motion, and use them for physically grounded control?

name: Cong Shen group (Cong Shen)
summary: The group studies RLHF theory, bandits and pure-exploration methods, including sampling strategies for preference-based fine-tuning.

question: How can robots learn from heterogeneous human demonstrations and coordinate with people?

name: CREST-ENSAE – Perchet (Vianney Perchet)
summary: Works on the theory of bandits, online learning and RL, including RL with transition lookahead and learning in markets.
question: What are the optimal ways to learn and decide online when feedback is partial and strategic?

name: Criteo AI Lab – sequential decision making (Marc Abeille)
summary: Industry research on bandit and RL theory, including exploration in linear bandits and learning in contextual and lookahead MDPs.
question: How can online systems explore efficiently with provable guarantees?

name: Csaba Szepesvári group (Csaba Szepesvári)
institution: University of Alberta; Amii; Google DeepMind
summary: The group creates and analyses algorithms for efficient sequential decision making, including bandit algorithms, RL theory and connections between RL and control.
question: How can algorithms learn efficiently and effectively in sequential decision making, with provable guarantees?

name: CSI-Agent Group (Honguk Woo)
institution: Sungkyunkwan University (Department of Computer Science and Engineering)
summary: The group builds embodied agents with reinforcement learning, including risk-sensitive and multi-objective offline RL, test-time world-model adaptation and incremental skill learning.
question: How can embodied agents perceive, reason and act reliably in changing physical and simulated environments?

name: CWI Machine Learning group – Koolen (Wouter M. Koolen)

summary: Develops provably safe reinforcement learning that combines set-based reachability analysis with action projection and shielding, applied to autonomous vehicles, robots and power systems.

name: Dabeen Lee group (Dabeen Lee)

question: How can decisions be made well when data arrive over time and constraints must be respected?

institution: University of Alberta; Amii; Google DeepMind
primary: RL foundations and RL for reasoning
summary: The group works on foundations of RL and representation learning, including spectral representations for RL and reinforcement learning for language-model reasoning.

name: Daniel Russo group (Daniel Russo)
summary: The group studies exploration, Thompson sampling and policy optimisation in sequential decision making.
question: How should an agent explore to learn good decisions efficiently?

summary: Develops model-based RL agents that learn world models and train inside them (Dreamer series), now applied to robots at a stealth start-up founded after leaving Google DeepMind in late 2025.

question: How can learning systems, including RL agents, be made robust, safe and trustworthy?

name: Data Mining and Machine Learning group (Sebastian Tschiatschek)
summary: Studies optimization and representation problems in deep RL, such as plasticity loss and hyperbolic representations, and rule-guided policy evaluation and improvement.
question: Why does training of deep RL agents become unstable or lose plasticity, and how can it be made reliable?

name: Data Science & AI Lab – dlab (Robert West)
summary: Develops RL-with-verifiable-rewards methods for language-model reasoning alongside work on NLP and AI safety.
question: How can AI systems be built that are safe for humanity, at the intersection of AI, NLP and computational social science?

name: Data Science in Mechanical Engineering – DSME (Sebastian Trimpe)
summary: The institute develops learning and control algorithms for physical machines, including safe and model-based reinforcement learning.
question: How can robots and other physical machines learn from limited real-world data while keeping guarantees on safety and performance?

name: Data to Actionable Knowledge Lab (Finale Doshi-Velez)
summary: The lab develops interpretable and off-policy reinforcement learning methods for healthcare decision support.
question: How can sequential decision models be made interpretable and safe enough to support clinical decisions?

name: Data-Driven Decision Making Lab, D3M (Scott Sanner)
summary: The lab works on sequential decision making alongside recommendation, including offline model-based planning, multi-agent RL and RL for traffic control.
question: How can rich sources of data be turned into optimal and actionable sequential decisions?

name: David Meger group (David Meger)
summary: The group works on reinforcement learning for robots, including off-policy value learning, goal-conditioned RL and distributional RL theory.
question: How can robots learn reliable control policies from interaction with reinforcement learning?

name: Daw Lab (Nathaniel Daw)
primary: model-based vs model-free RL in humans
summary: The lab uses computational, neural and behavioural methods to study how people and animals learn from rewards and punishments, including model-based planning, replay and successor representations.
question: How do people and animals learn from trial and error to make decisions in computationally demanding sequential tasks?

name: Debmalya Mandal (University of Warwick)
summary: Works on theoretical foundations of RL, including performative RL and corruption-robust RL from human feedback.
question: How should RL algorithms be designed when deployed policies change the environment they learn from?

name: Decision Intelligence Lab (Longbo Huang)
summary: The lab studies theory and algorithms for decision-making, including deep RL, RL theory, multi-agent flow policies and learning-augmented network optimization.
question: How can efficient, robust and safe AI theory and algorithms be developed for decision making and optimization in networked systems?

name: Decision Making Lab (Byung-Jun Lee)
summary: The lab works mainly on reinforcement learning, including offline and multi-objective RL with distribution-correction methods, diffusion planning and multi-agent simulators, plus industrial AI.
question: How can agents learn good decisions from fixed datasets and apply them to industrial problems?

name: Deep Reinforcement Learning Group, CASIA (Dongbin Zhao)
institution: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences (CASIA); UCAS
summary: The group studies deep and multi-agent RL and applies it to intelligent driving, embodied intelligence, game AI and agent training.

summary: Combines models of soft and compliant robots with RL to learn locomotion, jumping and whole-arm manipulation that exploits body dynamics.

lead: Dennis J. N. J. Soemers; Kurt Driessens
summary: Combines RL and search for game-playing agents, including self-play with non-neural learners and action-duration learning.
question: How can reinforcement learning and search be combined to build general game-playing agents?

name: Department of Computational Neuroscience (Peter Dayan)
institution: Max Planck Institute for Biological Cybernetics
summary: The department builds and tests computational models of how humans and animals learn to choose actions from rewards and punishments, including neuromodulation and neural reinforcement learning.
question: How do humans and other animals come to choose appropriate, and sometimes inappropriate, actions in the face of rewards and punishments?

name: Dependable Computing Laboratory (Wenchao Li)
summary: The lab works on safe and specification-guided reinforcement learning, including offline safe RL, temporal-logic generalisation and multi-agent RL with control barrier functions.
question: How can learning-enabled systems satisfy formal safety and task specifications?

name: Dependable Control and Decision Group – DECODE (Giancarlo Ferrari-Trecate)
summary: Develops policy parametrizations and learning methods for neural controllers with built-in stability guarantees, including stability-constrained RL.
question: How can learning-based controllers become more autonomous and self-adapting while remaining dependable?

name: Dhawale Lab — neural algorithms for learning
institution: Indian Institute of Science, Centre for NeuroScience
summary: The lab studies how neural circuits learn complex motor skills. Its IISc project with Ambedkar Dukkipati analyzes rodent learning using reinforcement learning models, neural recordings and perturbations in continuous action spaces.

summary: Works on reinforcement learning theory and algorithms, including model-based exploration, robustness and RL fine-tuning of language models.
question: How can reinforcement learning be made sample-efficient, robust and safe for real autonomous systems?

name: Dimitrakakis Group (Christos Dimitrakakis)
summary: Studies Bayesian and inverse RL, bandit learning in games and matching markets, and fairness and privacy in sequential decision-making.
question: How can agents make approximately optimal sequential decisions under uncertainty while respecting constraints such as fairness and privacy?

name: Disney Research – Robotics, Zurich (Moritz Bächer)
summary: Trains expressive locomotion, motion-tracking and falling policies with deep RL for legged and animated robotic characters using GPU simulation.
question: How can RL bring animated characters to life as physical robots with stylized yet robust motion?

name: Doina Precup group (Doina Precup)
summary: The group works on reinforcement learning, temporal abstraction (options), and reasoning and planning under uncertainty, with applications in medicine and control.
question: How can agents use temporal abstraction and planning to learn and act under uncertainty?

name: EMERGE Lab (Eugene Vinitsky)

name: Emma Brunskill group
summary: Develops sample-efficient and offline RL methods, including off-policy evaluation with confidence intervals, for education and healthcare applications.

name: Eric Eaton group (Eric Eaton)
summary: The group studies lifelong and continual learning for reinforcement learning, replicable RL and stable high-update-ratio deep RL.

name: Eric Mazumdar group (Eric Mazumdar)

question: How should learning algorithms behave when they interact with other strategic learners and people?

name: Eric Moulines (RL and stochastic approximation theory)
summary: Proves convergence and sample-complexity results for policy gradient, actor-critic and Q-learning methods via stochastic approximation.
question: What finite-sample guarantees can be proven for RL algorithms built on stochastic approximation?

name: Ernst group – RL and energy (Damien Ernst)

question: How can RL solve complex decision and control problems, especially in energy systems?

teamMembers.role: Full-time researcher at ULiège since 2024 (group roster labels postdoctoral researcher)

name: Fei Fang group
summary: Combines machine learning and multi-agent systems, including multi-agent RL from human feedback and RL training of language models.
question: How can reinforcement learning and multi-agent reinforcement learning be combined with large language models for multi-agent decision-making?

name: Foster Lab (David Foster)
summary: The lab records hippocampal place-cell sequences in rodents to study how replay of experience relates to goals, reward signalling by dopamine and planning of future paths.
question: How does hippocampal replay of past and possible paths support memory and goal-directed navigation?

name: Foundation Model and Reinforcement Learning Research Lab (FMRL2) (Banghua Zhu)
summary: Works on RL for foundation models, including reward-model evaluation for RLHF and large-scale asynchronous RL for long-horizon search agents.
question: How can reinforcement learning and open infrastructure make frontier foundation models more efficient and safe?

name: Foundations of Artificial Intelligence – FAI (Jörg Hoffmann)
summary: The group combines AI planning with learned action policies, working on testing, verification and safe training of reinforcement-learned policies.
question: How can action policies learned by reinforcement learning be tested and verified so they are safe to use in planning problems?

name: Francesco Belardinelli (Imperial College London)
summary: Develops shielding and other formal-methods techniques for safe single- and multi-agent RL.
question: How can formal methods make reinforcement learning and multi-agent systems safe?

name: Furong Huang lab
summary: Studies foundation models as decision-making systems, using RL with verifiable rewards and reward modelling to train and align language, vision-language and embodied agents.
question: How can foundation models reason, act, recover from failure and improve as trustworthy decision-making systems?

name: Gabriele Farina group (Gabriele Farina)
summary: The group studies multi-agent learning and equilibrium computation, including policy-gradient methods for imperfect-information games.
question: How can learning dynamics compute equilibria in large imperfect-information games?

name: Game Innovation Lab (Julian Togelius)
primary: RL and open-ended learning in games
summary: Builds game-based environments and benchmarks for RL and open-ended learning, and trains RL agents for game playing and procedural level design.
question: How can AI systems design their own goals so as to learn surprising skills?

name: Game Theory group, AI Center (Viliam Lisý)
summary: Develops reinforcement learning and search algorithms for zero-sum imperfect-information games, including learned world models and test-time adaptation.
question: How can agents learn models and reason with them to play well in large imperfect-information games?

name: Gang Wang group (Gang Wang)
institution: Beijing Institute of Technology (School of Automation)
summary: The group applies control, optimisation and reinforcement learning to multi-agent and cyber-physical systems, including transformer world models (STORM) and modular world models for multi-task RL.
question: How can control, optimization and reinforcement learning be applied to multi-agent networks and cyber-physical systems?

name: General Robotics & AI Lab (GRAIL) (Lerrel Pinto)
institution: New York University; Meta Superintelligence Labs
summary: Works on robot learning, including reinforcement learning for adaptation, action and behavior modeling, and low-cost open-source robots.
question: How can robots learn general skills from data and adapt them in homes and other real environments?

teamMembers.name: Gaoyue Zhou
teamMembers.role: PhD student, co-advised with Yann LeCun

name: General Robotics Lab (Boyuan Chen)
summary: Builds robot learning methods including preference-driven RL with language-model feedback, self-imitation RL and RL-trained humanoid locomotion.
question: How can machines learn, act and collaborate by discovering how the world works?

teamMembers.name: Xinyuan Luo
teamMembers.role: PhD student, co-advised with Xianyi Cheng

name: Generalizable Robotics and AI Lab (GRAIL) (Lawson L.S. Wong)
summary: Studies state representations for robot learning and planning, including approximately equivariant RL architectures and on-robot RL with learned rewards.
question: Which intermediate state representations enable effective robot learning and planning, and therefore robot generalization?

name: Gergely Neu (UPF)
summary: Neu works on the theory of sequential decision making, proving regret and sample-complexity guarantees for reinforcement learning, bandit and online-optimization algorithms.
question: What are provably efficient algorithms and fundamental limits for sequential decision making in online optimization, bandits and reinforcement learning?

name: Gilles Stoltz (online learning and bandits)
summary: Works on online learning and contextual bandits, including RL-based expert policy orchestration.
question: How can sequential prediction and decision methods stay robust when data are adversarial or non-stationary?

name: Giovanni Montana (University of Warwick)
summary: Develops offline and offline-to-online RL methods, including for multi-agent settings.
question: How can RL and autonomous decision-making methods be developed from theory to real-world deployment?

name: Giuseppe De Giacomo (University of Oxford)
summary: Works on LTL/LTLf synthesis and planning, including the use of temporal-logic specifications to structure multi-task RL.
question: How can temporal-logic specifications be used to synthesise and guide the behaviour of agents, including RL agents?

name: Goal-Oriented Long-Lived Systems – GOALS (Nick Hawes)
summary: Develops planning and RL methods under uncertainty for long-lived mobile robots, including risk-aware and distributional RL and POMDP solvers.
question: How can robots operating for days, weeks or months in dynamic, uncertain environments perform better the longer they act?

teamMembers.name: Kate Lampo
teamMembers.role: MSc by Research student (official profile); listed in GOALS roster as student

name: Google DeepMind Robotics (Carolina Parada)
summary: Builds the Gemini Robotics vision-language-action and embodied-reasoning models and uses reinforcement learning among other training methods to improve robot dexterity.
question: How can a single generalist model let robots reason about and act in the physical world across many embodiments?

name: Google DeepMind – AlphaProof / RL for formal mathematics (Thomas Hubert)
summary: Develops AlphaProof, an AlphaZero-style RL and search system that proves olympiad-level mathematics in the Lean formal language, and follow-up proof-search systems for research mathematics.
question: Can reinforcement learning with formal verification reach and extend expert-level mathematical reasoning?

name: Google DeepMind – André Barreto
summary: Studies how RL problems can be decomposed into simpler tasks whose solutions are recombined, along with work on reward uncertainty, agency and plasticity in RL agents.
question: How can reinforcement learning problems be decomposed into simpler tasks whose solutions combine to solve the original problem quickly?

name: Google DeepMind – Hado van Hasselt
summary: Works on core deep RL algorithms, including Wasserstein policy optimisation and RL update rules discovered by meta-learning.
question: Can better reinforcement learning update rules be designed, or discovered automatically from the experience of many agents?

name: Google DeepMind – Will Dabney
summary: Works on distributional and deep RL methods and on links between RL and neuroscience, including distributional value coding in the brain.
question: What are the missing ingredients on the path from current deep RL agents to human-level learning, and what can the brain's value coding tell us about them?

name: Google – Paradigms of Intelligence team, Zurich (João Sacramento)
summary: Studies how sequence models trained with RL can explore through temporally abstract internal actions and reach cooperation among self-interested learning agents by in-context inference about co-players.
question: How can the in-context learning of sequence models support hierarchical exploration and cooperation among learning agents?

name: Graph Machine Learning Group (Cesare Alippi)
summary: Develops graph-based multi-agent RL methods, including message-passing policies and continual learning in non-stationary environments.
question: How can learning systems operate on graph-structured, non-stationary dynamical systems, including multi-agent RL?

name: Guanghui Lan group
summary: Designs stochastic optimization algorithms for reinforcement learning, such as policy and value mirror descent and auto-exploration methods for online RL.
question: How can efficient algorithms be designed for the optimization problems arising in reinforcement learning?

name: Gugan Thoppe group (Gugan Thoppe)
institution: Indian Institute of Science (Department of Computer Science and Automation)
summary: The group studies stochastic approximation and its use in reinforcement learning, including finite-time analysis of risk-sensitive RL algorithms.
question: What convergence guarantees can stochastic approximation methods give for reinforcement learning algorithms?

name: Ha Lab (Sehoon Ha)
primary: RL for legged and humanoid robots
summary: Applies reinforcement learning and world models to legged locomotion, humanoid robots and character animation.
question: How can robots learn agile and stable motor skills that transfer from simulation to the real world?

name: Haipeng Luo group (Haipeng Luo)
summary: The group studies online learning, bandits and reinforcement learning theory, including adversarial MDPs and learning in Markov games.
question: How can learners adapt to both stochastic and adversarial environments with optimal guarantees?

name: Hao Wang group (Hao Wang)
summary: The group applies machine learning, including constrained and interpretable actor-critic reinforcement learning, to smart grids and power and energy systems.
question: How can machine learning and reinforcement learning make energy systems efficient and reliable?

name: Harada-Kurose-Mukuta Lab (Tatsuya Harada)
institution: The University of Tokyo (Graduate School of Information Science and Technology); RIKEN AIP
summary: Within its broader machine-intelligence work, the lab studies deep RL algorithms, including regularised policy optimisation, Bellman-operator variants, cross-embodiment offline RL and decoder-free world models.
question: How can intelligent systems that combine physical-world information with large data and computation be built?

name: Hartley Lab (Catherine Hartley)
summary: The lab characterises how learning, memory and value-based decision processes develop from childhood to adulthood, using reinforcement-learning models such as predictive representations.
question: How do the learning, memory and decision-making processes that shape behaviour change across development?

name: He Zhu group (He Zhu)
summary: The group combines programming-languages methods with reinforcement and imitation learning to learn verifiable, specification-compliant policies.
question: How can programmatic structure and formal constraints make learned policies reliable?

researchPlans.title: Research Statement: Neurosymbolic Robot Programming
researchPlans.author: He Zhu

name: Helmholtz Institute for Human-Centered AI (Eric Schulz)
summary: Studies exploration and learning from interaction in humans and machine agents, including the theory of goal-conditioned RL and skill learning.
question: What computational principles govern how humans and machines explore and learn from interaction?

name: Helping Hands Lab (Robert Platt)
summary: Develops perception, planning and learning methods, including symmetry-aware (equivariant) reinforcement learning, for robot manipulation in unstructured environments.
question: How can symmetry and structure make robot manipulation learning data-efficient?

name: Holroyd lab – cognitive control and reward (Clay Holroyd)
summary: Studies neural reward signals such as the reward positivity and the role of anterior cingulate cortex in reward-driven, hierarchically organized behavior.
question: How does the brain use reward signals to learn and control hierarchically organized behavior?

name: Honghao Wei group (Honghao Wei)
summary: The group works on safe and constrained reinforcement learning, including safe RLHF and online constrained MDPs.
question: How can learning agents optimise rewards while satisfying safety constraints throughout learning?

name: Hsiu-Chin Lin group (Hsiu-Chin Lin)
summary: The group works on robot learning and control, including safe RL with recovery, value learning and world models for cross-embodiment quadrupedal locomotion.
question: How can robots learn safe and robust control policies for locomotion and manipulation?

name: Huawei Noah's Ark Lab Paris (Balázs Kégl)
summary: Industry research on decentralized hierarchical multi-agent RL and on reward-based training objectives for generative models.
question: How can learning agents be organized hierarchically to control complex systems?

name: Huazheng Wang group (Huazheng Wang)
summary: The group studies bandits and reinforcement learning under misspecification and adversarial reward corruption, and builds RL environments for energy demand response.
question: How can interactive learning algorithms stay reliable under misspecification and adversarial feedback?

name: Human and Machine Cognition Lab (Charley Wu)
summary: The lab uses reinforcement-learning-inspired computational models and behavioural experiments to study how humans explore, learn and use social information.
question: How do people make efficient use of limited cognitive resources to explore and learn, including from other people, and what can machine learning take from this?

name: Human Reinforcement Learning team (Stefano Palminteri)
summary: Characterizes the computational processes and biases of human RL, such as relative value encoding and asymmetric learning rates.
question: Which computational processes and biases govern how humans learn from rewards and punishments?

name: Human-Robot Interfaces and Interaction Lab – HRI² (Arash Ajoudani)
summary: The lab works on physical human-robot interaction and uses safe and sim-to-real reinforcement learning for contact-rich manipulation and legged locomotion.
question: How can robots physically interact and collaborate with humans safely and adaptively?

name: Humanoid Robots Lab (Maren Bennewitz)
summary: The lab develops perception, planning and learning methods for robots, including constraint-aware and multi-objective reinforcement learning.
question: How can robots perceive, plan and act autonomously in cluttered and dynamic real-world environments?

name: Hybrid Robotics Group (Koushil Sreenath)
summary: Uses RL and model-based control to produce dynamic, robust locomotion and manipulation on bipedal, humanoid and quadrupedal robots.
question: How can legged robots achieve versatile, dynamic and robust behaviour through learning and control?

name: Hybrid Systems Laboratory (Claire Tomlin)
summary: Combines Hamilton-Jacobi reachability and safety filtering with learning, including residual RL for safe humanoid control.
question: How can learning-enabled autonomous systems be given provable safety guarantees?

name: ICAROS Lab (Stefanos Nikolaidis)
summary: Combines computational human-robot interaction with quality-diversity search and RL to train agents that coordinate with novel partners and to generate test scenarios.
question: How can robots continuously adapt their actions through simulated and real-world experience when interacting with people?

name: ICON Lab (Negar Mehr)
summary: Develops control and learning algorithms for interacting autonomous agents, including multi-agent RL credit assignment and the exploitability of multi-agent imitation learning.
question: How can autonomous systems safely and intelligently interact with each other and with humans?

researchPlans.title: Towards Fast, Flexible, and Data-Efficient Algorithms for Multi-Agent Interaction

name: Ida Momennejad (Microsoft Research NYC)
summary: Studies how natural and artificial agents build internal models for memory and planning, combining RL, human behavioural experiments and evaluation of reasoning in language models.
question: How do learning, memory, reasoning and agency interact to support flexible planning in natural and artificial intelligence?

name: IDEAL Lab (Washim Uddin Mondal)
institution: Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur (Department of Electrical Engineering)
summary: The lab works on theoretical reinforcement learning, including global convergence of policy-gradient and actor-critic methods for average-reward and robust RL, and multi-agent learning.
question: What convergence and sample-complexity guarantees can policy-gradient and actor-critic methods achieve?

name: IDLab – AI for energy (Chris Develder)
summary: Applies RL, often combined with model predictive control, to demand response, battery and EV charging control in power systems.
question: How can learning-based control manage flexible energy assets in power systems efficiently and reliably?

name: IDLab – Simoens group (Pieter Simoens)
summary: Studies RL agents through the lens of cognitive science, including interval timing, policy compression and inverse RL for alignment.
question: Which cognitive mechanisms, such as timing and resource limits, can make RL agents behave more like humans and animals?

researchPlans.title: 2025 thesis proposal: Cooperation between RL agents with non-exponential reward discounting
researchPlans.author: Pieter Simoens

name: IKIDA – Interactive AI Algorithms and Cognitive Models (Dorothea Koert)
summary: The group studies interactive reinforcement learning with human input and policy blending for multi-agent coexistence in human-robot settings.
question: How can robots learn interactively from human input while handling unreliable advice and coexisting with other agents?

name: ILIAD (Dorsa Sadigh)
summary: Develops algorithms for agents that interact with humans and other agents, including preference-based reward learning and RL for robot policies.
question: How can AI agents safely and reliably interact with people and other agents?

name: Improbable AI Lab (Pulkit Agrawal)
primary: RL for robot locomotion and manipulation
summary: Builds machines that learn continuously from interaction, using reinforcement learning for locomotion, dexterous manipulation and continual learning.
question: How can machines automatically and continuously learn about their environment?

name: Ineffable Intelligence (David Silver)
summary: Start-up David Silver founded after leaving Google DeepMind (announced January 2026) to build RL systems that learn from their own experience rather than from human data.
question: Can a learning system discover knowledge and skills entirely from its own experience, without human data?

name: Information and Network Dynamics Lab – INDY (Matthias Grossglauser)
summary: Develops hierarchical and causal RL and dueling-bandit methods that combine reward and preference feedback.
question: How can large dynamical systems involving human and technical agents be modelled and controlled from data?

name: Inria Argo – Bušić (Ana Bušić)
summary: Studies optimization, control and learning for energy networks, including delayed cooperative multi-agent RL and wind farm control benchmarks.
question: How can learning-based control coordinate many agents in energy networks with renewables?

name: Inria Flowers (Pierre-Yves Oudeyer; Clément Moulin-Frier)
summary: Studies curiosity-driven, autotelic RL agents that set their own goals, including LLM-based agents and artificial societies.
question: Which mechanisms enable open-ended, curiosity-driven learning and development in humans and machines?

researchPlans.title: Language and culture internalization for human-like autotelic AI
researchPlans.author: Cédric Colas, Tristan Karch, Clément Moulin-Frier, and Pierre-Yves Oudeyer

name: Inria NEO – Avrachenkov (Konstantin Avrachenkov)
summary: Studies the structure of optimal policies in MDPs and POMDPs and learning in restless bandits.
question: Which structural properties of stochastic decision problems make optimal policies efficient to learn and compute?

name: Inria POLARIS (Nicolas Gast; Bruno Gaujal)
summary: Develops learning and control for large stochastic systems, including restless bandits, Whittle indices and regret in average-reward MDPs.
question: How can mean-field and stochastic models give efficient, provable learning algorithms for large Markov decision processes?

name: Inria Scool (Philippe Preux; Odalric-Ambrym Maillard; Emilie Kaufmann; Riad Akrour)
lead: Philippe Preux; Odalric-Ambrym Maillard; Emilie Kaufmann; Riad Akrour
institution: Inria Lille / Université de Lille / CNRS
summary: Studies sequential decision making under uncertainty through bandit and RL problems, from theory to applications in health, agriculture and ecology.
question: How should an agent make sequential decisions under uncertainty, and with what guarantees?

name: Inria Sierra – Bach (Francis Bach)
summary: Contributes optimization and learning theory to RL post-training of language models, including RLHF alignment collapse and advantage weighting.
question: Which optimization principles explain the behavior of RL post-training for large models?

name: Inria Thoth – Gaillard (Pierre Gaillard)
summary: Works on online learning theory, including reset-free online MDPs, convex RL and multinomial logistic MDPs.
question: Which regret guarantees can online learning methods achieve in sequential decision problems?

name: Inria Willow (Justin Carpentier)
summary: Develops RL methods that exploit physics and differentiable simulation, including survival-based goal-conditioned RL and Sobolev RL.
question: How can robots reason about and act in the physical world by combining physics-based models with learning?

name: INSAIT 3D vision group (Danda Pani Paudel)
summary: Applies reinforcement learning to vision tasks, including agentic RL for controllable 3D scene generation and policy optimization of diffusion models.
question: How can RL-trained agents and models generate and reason about 3D scenes from vision and language?

name: InstaDeep Decision-Making Research (Arnu Pretorius)
summary: The team develops reinforcement learning methods, including scalable sequence models for multi-agent RL and RL-based solvers for routing problems.
question: How can reinforcement learning agents scale to many-agent coordination and industrial decision problems?

name: Institute for Machine Learning (Sepp Hochreiter)
summary: Works on reward redistribution for credit assignment, extending the RUDDER line to reasoning models, and on recurrent xLSTM-based large action models trained offline.
question: How can rewards be redistributed and sequence models built so that agents assign credit efficiently over long horizons?

name: Institute of Machine Learning and Neural Computation – Maass group (Wolfgang Maass)
summary: Models how biological neural circuits and plasticity rules such as behavioral time-scale plasticity can implement successor-relation based reinforcement learning and goal-directed planning.
question: How do plasticity rules in biological neural networks support learning of cognitive maps and goal-directed decisions?

name: Intelligent Autonomous Systems Lab (Jan Peters)
summary: The lab develops reinforcement learning, policy search and imitation learning methods for robot motor skills, manipulation and control on real hardware.
question: How can robots learn motor and manipulation skills from interaction that are fast, stable and reliable enough for real hardware?

name: Intelligent Control and Tele-science Research Center (Xueqian Wang)
summary: The centre works on intelligent robots, including deep reinforcement learning methods such as offline safe-policy fine-tuning with world models and robust offline-to-online RL.
question: How can robots learn control policies with deep reinforcement learning that remain safe and robust?

name: Intelligent Control Systems Group (Melanie Zeilinger)
summary: Combines model predictive control with learning, including RL and online model learning, to obtain controllers with safety guarantees for uncertain systems.
question: How can high-performance learning-based control be made safe for systems that act in uncertain environments and interact with humans?
